claim: Table S4's ruled grid provides FOUR (Average efficiency, SD) column pairs but only THREE lipidoid:DOPE ratios are labelled. The raw text layer therefore reads '... Average SD / efficienc y (%)', an apparently orphaned header.
locus_A: SI p.18, Table S4 header rule at y=330.24: the drawn rule segments into 9 column bands (name + 4 efficiency/SD pairs). Header row y=345.2 carries FOUR 'Average' labels at x0 = 136.0, 262.4, 382.3, 508.9 but only THREE 'Lipidoid:DOPE=' labels at x0 = 136.0, 262.4, 382.3.
locus_B: SI p.18, Table S4 body: every lipidoid row's first value sits at x0 ~ 211.7 (band 133.08-226.68); the L2K row's two values sit alone at x0 = 525.8 and 557.2 (bands 506.16-545.64 and 546.00-572.28).
measurement_that_settled_it: Measured by x position, not by reading order. The fourth, unlabelled pair is an L2K-ONLY column: the control was measured at no DOPE ratio. stage05_values.py asserts that the six ratio cells of the L2K row are empty and that the control cells of every lipidoid row are empty; both hold.
what_we_emitted: L2K's Table S4 value is recorded with formulation 'n/a (control)'. A reading-order parser would have assigned 14.0 +/- 1.8 to lipidoid:DOPE = 2:1.
severity: changes values if mis-read; no value changed here

claim: The SI uses TWO different mass conventions and labels only one of them. Table S1's 'calc.' column is the NEUTRAL monoisotopic mass; the HRMS sections' 'calculated m/z' is the protonated ion [M+H]+.
locus_A: SI pp.4-5, Table S1: the '(M+H+)' annotation appears ONLY under the 'observed' column, never under 'calc.'. Amine 1 + C12, 1 tail: calc. 282.3, observed 283.5.
locus_B: SI pp.9/12/15: 'HR-MS (ESI): m/z = 451.4987 [M + H+], calculated m/z = 451.4986' for 1C12-D.
measurement_that_settled_it: Our computed neutral exact mass for amine 1 + one C12 is 282.3035 (residual +0.0035 Da vs their calc), while our [M+H]+ is 283.3108 (residual -1.0073 Da, i.e. exactly one proton). Separately, our computed [M+H]+ for 1C12-D is 451.49858 vs their HRMS calc 451.4986, -0.024 mDa. The two conventions are therefore both correct and different.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. Both columns are verification-only; no emitted value depends on a mass. Recorded because the first version of stage01_blocks.py compared our [M+H]+ to Table S1's calc column and reported a 1.0421 Da residual. Under a 2 Da tolerance every row would have 'passed' one proton out.
severity: would have changed structure verification; caught before use

claim: 1C12-D's 1H NMR text listing prints '0.86 (t, J = 6.9 Hz, 3H)' for the terminal methyls, but the compound is N,N-DIdodecyl and must have 6H there.
locus_B: SI p.8, the SPECTRUM's own printed integrals on the same page: 2.16, 4.10, 2.59, 3.50, 3.64, 40.83, 6.38 -- the methyl integrates 6.38, and the set sums to 63.2 H.
measurement_that_settled_it: The molecular formula is C30H62N2 = 62 H, printed by the authors themselves under the drawing on SI p.7 ('Chemical Formula: C30H62N2'). The text listing is 3 H short -- exactly one methyl group. The figure integral 6.38 and the formula both say 6H. The same gate agrees exactly for 1C16-D (78 vs 78) and is off by 1 for 1C16-S (45 vs 46, the exchangeable N-H), so the discrepancy is specific to this one listing.
what_we_emitted: The structure, unchanged: N,N-didodecyl. It is a printing error in the paper's text, not a structural doubt. Gate Q-6b is declared to agree on 2 of 3 and fails if that changes.
severity: cosmetic in the paper; would have changed the structure if the text had been believed over the figure

claim: The SI's own List of Contents omits every transfection-efficiency table -- that is, the entire value payload of the document.
locus_A: SI p.2, 'List of Contents': lists Table S1 (p.4), Table S2 (p.6), NMR and HRMS (p.7), Figure S1 (p.16), Figure S2 (p.17). Five items.
locus_B: SI pp.18-19 carry Tables S3, S4, S5 and S6, captioned 'The average transfection efficiency (the percentage of transfected cells) corresponds to Figure 2A / Figure 3 / Figure 6 / Figure 8'. None is listed on p.2.
measurement_that_settled_it: Read directly from the text layer: the four captions exist on pp.18-19 and the contents page ends at Figure S2. 87 of the SI's 87 delivery values live in the four unlisted tables.
what_we_emitted: All 87 values come from the unlisted tables. Recorded because a triage that trusted the contents page would have concluded this SI holds no delivery endpoint at all and returned zero rows.
severity: would have caused a false zero

claim: Tables S5 and S6 report different values for the same two purified compounds.
measurement_that_settled_it: Ratio measured against the best Table S5 150 ng cell for each compound: 1C16-S 2.0/0.4 = 5.00x; 1C16-D 11.3/7.0 = 1.61x. Against the 1:2 cell, 1C16-S's ratio is unbounded (0.0 denominator). Table S6 prints NO lipidoid:DOPE ratio, so the panels may not describe the same formulation.
what_we_emitted: Each panel's own value, with its source_table named on the row. Nothing is averaged or reconciled across panels. DECISIONS.md D-6.
severity: changes values if panels were pooled

claim: The CRUDE 1C16 mixture out-performs both of its own purified components.
locus_B: SI p.19, Table S6: purified 1C16-D = 11.3 +/- 1.4 %, purified 1C16-S = 2.0 +/- 0.1 %.
measurement_that_settled_it: Both read from the text layer. Not a contradiction -- the paper's own Figure 8 point is that a 1C16-S : 1C16-D blend (1:2) reaches 26.1 %, above either component. It is recorded because it is direct evidence that a crude library member is NOT interchangeable with any single structure in it.
what_we_emitted: Nothing. It is the reason the 12 crude entries are not emitted with a structure.

claim: SUSPECTED: Table S1's 'calc.' column is [M+H]+, making our amine-1 masses wrong by ~1 Da.
severity: Retired by C-2's measurement: comparing our NEUTRAL mass instead gives residuals [0.0348, -0.0461, 0.0035, -0.0087] Da, and the HRMS section independently confirms [M+H]+ to -0.024 mDa. The residual was the proton, not an error.

claim: SUSPECTED: Table S1 has 25 (amine, alkyl halide) rows.
locus_A: stage01_blocks.py's first declared row count (a guess made before parsing).
measurement_that_settled_it: Measured: 23 rows -- 17 on p.4 and 6 on p.5. The assertion caught the guess. The library SHAPE (20 amines x 10 alkyl halides = 200) is asserted instead, because that is the claim the tracker and the manuscript would cite.

claim: SUSPECTED: 1C12-D might be MONO-alkylated, since its 1H text prints 3H for the terminal methyl.
measurement_that_settled_it: Retired three ways: our computed [M+H]+ for the DI compound matches their HRMS calc at -0.053 ppm; the authors' own drawn formula is C30H62N2; and the unprinted relation (their 1C16-D m/z) - (their 1C12-D m/z) = 112.12518 equals 2 x C4H8 = 112.12520 (-0.0205 mDa), which only closes if BOTH are di-alkylated. Additionally the drawn bond count on SI p.7 is 32, matching the di-alkyl structure exactly.

claim: SUSPECTED (and WRONG, and silent): Table S5's DNA-amount label marks the LAST row of its dose block.
locus_A: stage05_values.py first version grouped rows by flushing at each DNA label, producing a clean-looking 30-row table with no error.
measurement_that_settled_it: The label is a MERGED CELL and its glyph is vertically centred: measured at row 6 of each 10-row block, in all three blocks. The first grouping stamped 1C12-D's 75 ng values (32.6 / 40.3 / 3.4) as 150 ng and cascaded through both later blocks -- 9 of 30 values on the wrong dose. Caught by reading the emitted CSV against the page, not by any check. Now asserted structurally (block runs 1C16-D:DOPE=2:1 -> L2K, exactly 10 rows, exactly one label, on row 6).
what_we_emitted: the corrected dose assignment, independently corroborated: the 150 ng block's L2K is 14.0 +/- 1.8, which is exactly the L2K printed in Tables S3, S4 and S6.
severity: would have changed the dose on 9 of 30 values
